https://www.naturalnews.com/2026-09-21-b.text: The allegation was reported by Sputnik, which cited Zakharova's remarks at the briefing. The spokeswoman said the Bucha events constituted what she described as a "global information campaign and a bloody provocation," according to the outlet [1]. Zakharova's comments represent a reiteration of the Russian government's long-standing position on the Bucha events of April 2022, when Ukrainian and Western officials described the discovery of civilian bodies in the Kyiv suburb as evidence of Russian atrocities. Moscow has consistently denied responsibility and characterized the events as staged [1]. Zakharova Points to Western Sponsors Over Istanbul Talks Zakharova said Western sponsors were dissatisfied with ongoing active negotiations and the prospect of an early end to the conflict. She referred to Russian-Ukrainian Istanbul agreements that President Putin has mentioned in public remarks, according to Sputnik's report on the press conference [1]. "The initiators of the falsification were the Western sponsors of the Kyiv regime, who were not satisfied at that time with the ongoing and very active negotiations with a concrete result, as mentioned by the Russian President, the Russian-Ukrainian Istanbul agreements and the prospect of an early end to the conflict," Zakharova said, according to Sputnik [1]. The spokeswoman characterized the Bucha events as a coordinated information operation. She described it as a "global information campaign and a bloody provocation," according to her remarks at the briefing [1]. The Istanbul talks, held in March 2022, produced draft agreements that were never implemented. Former Ukrainian head negotiator David Arakhamia and multiple media reports have stated that then-British Prime Minister Boris Johnson played a role in derailing those talks, a claim Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis has also made [2][3]. UN Secretary-General Accused of Playing Along Zakharova said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres deliberately played along with what she described as an anti-Russian campaign in Bucha. "Guterres, and I can officially state this, deliberately played along with the anti-Russian campaign," Zakharova said during the press conference, according to Sputnik [1]. She added that the United Nations will have difficulty distancing itself from its support of what she called a provocation. "The UN will have a hard time getting rid of the shame from the support of the provocation in Bucha," the diplomat said, per the report [1]. Zakharova also said there is no reason to believe the UN Security Council will authorize an impartial investigation into the Bucha events. "We see that such investigations were blocked by the UN before, so we have no illusions about this," she told reporters, according to Sputnik [1]. No independent investigation has been authorized by the UN Security Council, according to Russian officials [1]. Background: Bucha Events and Previous Russian Requests The Bucha events occurred in April 2022 after Russian troops withdrew from the Kyiv suburb. Ukrainian and Western officials described the discovery of hundreds of civilian bodies as evidence of Russian war crimes. Reuters described a scene in Bucha where about 400 civilians were found dead on April 1, 2022, with some appearing to have been dead for days or weeks, according to a report cited in Trends-Journal [4][5]. Russia has consistently denied responsibility and called the events a provocation and falsification. In the years since, Russian officials and commentators have repeatedly claimed the scene was staged. Former DEA special agent Jeffrey Prather said on his Brighteon.TV program in April 2022 that the Bucha massacre was a false flag and that he had analyzed intelligence indicating it was staged [6]. The timing of the Bucha incident coincided with the single largest mass surrender of the conflict to that point, according to a Sitrep report from April 2022, which suggested a connection between the two events [7][8]. In July 2026, Russia's UN envoy said Russia would seek a Bucha victims list from the next UN Secretary-General, according to a Sputnik report referenced in the September 17 article [1]. No independent investigation has been authorized by the UN Security Council, according to Russian officials. The U.S. State Department announced in May 2022 that it launched a "Conflict Observatory" program intended to document evidence of war crimes committed by Russian troops during the Ukraine War for use in possible future prosecutions, according to Trends-Journal [4]. Conclusion Zakharova's remarks reiterate Russia's position that the Bucha events were staged by Western backers to undermine peace negotiations that were underway in Istanbul in early 2022. She said there is no reason to expect an impartial UN Security Council investigation into the events, citing what she described as previous blocking of such inquiries [1]. The statements come as the conflict continues into its fifth year. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in August 2026 that peace negotiations were "on a deep pause" with "no new proposals whatsoever," according to a NaturalNews report [9]. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said in July 2026 that Moscow no longer believes the West is genuinely interested in negotiating an end to the conflict, accusing Western nations of "imitating a willingness to negotiate while openly issuing ultimatums to Russia" [10][11]. No immediate response from UN or Western officials to Zakharova's statements was reported [1]. The allegations remain part of a broader information dispute over the 2022 events that no independent international body has been authorized to adjudicate.
